Create a python class named Number with the following attributes.

Object Variable num_list stores a list of integers

Functions display() displays all the numbers in a row add(n) adds n to each number in the list

When an object is created from the class, it will ask user to input a list of integers in a row and initialise variable num_list with the values.

1 0 3 5 67 2 0

﻿Create a python class named Number with the following attributes.

Object Variable

    num
            stores an integer

Functions

    display()
            displays the integer

    swap(obj)
            takes in an object and swap the object variable value with its own

When an object is created from the class, it will initialise variable num with the value.

Write a program to perform the following:

1. Ask user to input an integer and create an object from the class.

2. Ask user to input another integer and create a second object from the class.

3. Call display() of object1 followed by object2.

4. Call swap() of object1 by passing in object2.

5. Call display() of object1 followed by object2.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Save snippet as: 3049.3.e3 Train

A train consists of carriages chained together with links. The carriages can have different sizes. Each carriage is represented by a series of "#" and a link is represented by a "-". In the example below, there are 3 carriages of sizes 5, 3 and 4 forming the train: #####-###-####

Write a python class named Train with the following attributes:

Class Variable total_carriage stores total number of carriages total_size stores total size of all the carriages

Object Variable carriage_list stores a list of carriage sizes forming the train

Functions input_list() ask user to input a list of carriage sizes (from 1 to 10) and save to carriage_list it will also update total_carriage and total_size. display() displays the following: 1. the train formed with "#" and "-" as illustrated above 2. total_carriage 3. total_size

Write a program to create 2 objects from the class. For each object, call input_list() followed by display().

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input

5 5 5 4 3 5 1 6

3 6 1 6 9 6 2

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the example below:

Example 1 Input carriage sizes (1- 10): 5 5 5 #####-#####-##### total carriages 3 total size 15 Input carriage sizes (1- 10): 4 3 5 1 6 ####-###-#####-#-###### total carriages 8 total size 34

Example 2 Input sizes (1- 10): 3 6 1 ###-######-# total carriages 3 total size 10 Input carriage sizes(1- 10): 6 9 6 2 ######-#########-######-## total carriages 7 total size 33

Save snippet as: 3050.2.e2 Racer

Certain cultures believe certain numbers are less lucky than others. The Chinese, for example, commonly consider 4 to be unlucky due to its Chinese pronunciation. You decided to investigate by creating a program to see if number 4 will always lose in a race.

Write a python class named Racer with the following attributes:

Class Variable: track_length set it to 30. It represents the track length.

Object Variables: racer_num stores the racer number distance stores the distance travelled in a race

Functions: race() add a random number (1 to 3) to distance each time it is called. if it exceeds track_length, set it to track_length. display() display position of racer on the screen with one space per unit travelled followed by racer_num and a " : " character at track_length spaces away if racer has not reached there.

Static Methods: winner(racer_list) takes in a list of Racer objects and determine the winners. A racer wins when its reaches the end point ":". If there are winners (can be more than 1), all winners will be displayed and True is returned. Otherwise it will return False. main() It will perform the following: 1. Create a list of 4 objects from the class with racer number 1 to 4. 2. Before the race starts: a. clear the screen b. call display() of each racer c. pause for 3 seconds. 3. Start the race by doing the following repeatedly: a. call race() of each racer. b. call display() of each racer and pause for 0.5 sec c. call winner(racer_list) to display winners if any d. end program when there is at least a winner

Run Racer.main().

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint:

You may use the following command to clear the screen:

import os # For Windows os.system('cls') # For macOS and Linux os.system('clear')

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Note that your results may differ as they are random.

The race begins like this 1 : 2 : 3 : 4 :

the racers will race towards the ":" 1 : 2 : 3 : 4 :

and ends when any racer reaches or surpass the end 1 : 2 3 : 4 Winner(s): Racer 2 Racer 4

Save snippet as: 3051.1.e3 Multiple Classes

You are using multiple classes to create a program for superheroes to compete in an arena. Your program will randomly choose 2 superheroes and their combat actions each round.

Create a class named Superhero with the following variables: name <- name of the character combat <- stores the next action: "attacks" or "defends"

The class will have a function select_combat() to decide if it will attack or defend during a combat: 1. It will generate a random number from 1 to 2. 2. If the random number is 1, set combat to "attacks", otherwise set it to "defends". The object initialisation will be Superhero(name).

Create a class named Arena with 2 static functions:

fight(hero_list) It takes in a list of Superhero objects and performs the following: 1. Randomly select 2 different heroes and call the their select_combat() function to set their combat action for the next round. 2. Display the result (e.g. Hulk attack vs Black Widow defend) 3. Repeat step (1) to (2) three times.

main() It performs the following: 1. Ask user to input a hero name. 2. Create an object from Superhero class and add it to a list. 4. Repeat step (1) to (2) until user enters "end" for the hero name. 5. Call fight() function to run the combat with the list of heroes for 3 rounds.

Run Arena.main().

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input

Spiderman Iron Man Black Widow end

Hulk Thor Captain America Black Widow end

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below: Your result may differ due to random numbers

Example 1 Hero name: Spiderman Hero name: Iron Man Hero name: Black Widow Hero name: end Spiderman attacks vs Black Widow attacks Iron Man defends vs Black Widow attacks Black Widow attacks vs Spiderman defends

Example 2 Hero name: Hulk Hero name: Thor Hero name: Captain America Hero name: Black Widow Hero name: end Hulk attacks vs Black Widow attacks Thor defends vs Captain America attacks Black Widow defends vs Hulk defends

Save snippet as: 3051.2.e2 Parent Child

The following shows the execution of a program: square = Square() square.input_length() square.calculate_area() square.display_area() circle = Circle() circle.input_radius() circle.calculate_area() circle.display_area()

Create the following classes to support the program above: 1. a class named Shape with a variable to store the area and a function display_area() to display the area. 2. a class named Square that inherits Shape and has a variable to store the length. It has two functions, input_length() to ask user to input the length and calculate_area() to calculate the area corrected up to 2 decimal places. 3. a class named Circle that inherits Shape and has a variable to store the radius. It has two functions, input_radius() to ask user to input the radius and calculate_area() to calculate the area corrected up to 2 decimal places.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input

9.5 4

11 22

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter length of square: 9.5 The area is 90.25 Enter radius of circle: 4 The area is 50.27

Example 2 Enter length of square: 11 The area is 121.0 Enter radius of circle: 22 The area is 1520.53

Create the following classes: 1. a class named Square that has a variable to store the length and a function square_area() to calculate and return the square area. 2. a class named Circle that has a variable to store the radius and a function circle_area() to calculate and return the circle area. 3. a class named Shape that inherits both Square and Circle and a function total_area() that calls the parent functions and compute the total area. Save snippet as: 3052.2.e1 Operations

You want to create intelligent plus and minus functions that can automatically detect if you are adding or subtracting strings or integers so that they can produce the right results.

Write a python class named NumOperation with the following attributes:

Object Variable x, y stores 2 input strings

Functions add() returns the value of x + y subtract() returns the value of x - y

Create a python class named StrOperation which inherits NumOperation and overrides the function subtract(). The function will subtract the first occurrence of string y from string x if it exists (eg. if x = "ABCDEF" and y = "CDE", then x - y = "ABF"). Otherwise, the subtraction does not change x.

Write a program that does the following: 1. Ask the user to input x and y 2. If x and y contain only digits (not even negative sign), create an object from NumOperation. Otherwise, create an object from StrOperation. 3. Call the functions add() and subtract() and display the results in the format shown in the test output.

Note that NumOperation will initialise x and y as integers whereas StrOperation will initialise them as strings when the object is created.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint: - recall isdigit() and find() from previous steps

Test Input

100 5

abc100 100

100abc 100

abc100abc abc

abcd cde

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the example below: Example 1 Enter x: 100 Enter y: 5 100 + 5 = 105 100 - 5 = 95

Example 2 Enter x: abc100 Enter y: 100 abc100 + 100 = abc100100 abc100 - 100 = abc

Example 3 Enter x: 100abc Enter y: 100 100abc + 100 = 100abc100 100abc - 100 = abc

Example 4 Enter x: abc100abc Enter y: abc abc100abc + abc = abc100abcabc abc100abc - abc = 100abc

Example 5 Enter x: abcd Enter y: cde abcd + cde = abcdcde abcd - cde = abcd
